DILG BAGONG PWP'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph OILG OPINION NO S. JUL 0 1 2025 HON. SUSAN V. ESCOTE Municipal Vice Mayor I Office of the Municipal Vice Mayor Bugasong, Antique Dear Hon. Escote: This refers to your Letter dated May 19, 2025 requesting legal guidance and clarification from this Department on the following matters: I. Is the suspension order of one-year which is reckoned to end on March 2026 as imposed by the Ombudsman against SP Victor, now Mayor-elect of Bugasong, Antique still legally in effect considering that such order was in relation to his official acts as SP Member of Antique and not as Mayor? 2. In the light of the provision of Section 46 of the Local Govemment Code ("LGC"), as premised by the Ombudsman order, does temporary vacancy exist for the position of Mayor of Bugasong, Antique by June 30, 2025 and does it necessitate the application of rule of succession for the said position? Attached to your letter is a copy of the Ombudsman Decision dated March 7, 2025, entitled Rey O. Ventura, et al. vs. Egidio R Elio, et al, wherein SP Victor Condez ("SP Victor") is among those found guilty of Grave Abuse of Authority, Grave Misconduct, and Conduct Unbecoming of a Public Officer. The dispositive portion of the Decision reads: "WHEREFORE, respondents Egidio P. Elio, Rony L. Molina, Victor R. Condez. Alfie Jay Q. Niquia, Plaridel E. Sanchez, IV, Mayella Mae P. Ladislao, Kenneth Dave B. Gasalao, and Julius Cezar O. Tajanlangit are hereby found GUILTY of Grave Abuse of Authority, Grave Misconduct and Conduct Unbecoming of a Public officer and. pursuant to Section IO. Rule Ill of Administrative Order No. 07, as amended, otherwise known as the Rules of Procedure of the Office of the Ombudsman, are meted the penalty of SUSPENSION FROM THE SERVICE WITHOUT PAY FOR ONE YEAR. In the event that the penalty of suspension cannot be imposed due to respondents' separation or retirement from the service, the alternative penalty of FINE equivalent to their respective basic salary for ONE (1) YEAR payable to the Office of the Ombudsman shall be imposed against them. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

The administrative charge of Gross Neglect of Duty is DISMISSED for lack of merit. SO ORDERED." We note however that the one-year Ombudsman's suspension order against SP Victor, among others, was issued and implemented during the election period, that is, within January 12, 2025 to June II, 2025.1 Also, the dispositive portion is bereft of any directive from the Ombudsman for this Department to implement the same, but only decreed SP Victor, among others, a one-year suspension from the service without pay, or an alternative penalty of fine equivalent to basic salary for one year payable to the Ombudsman "in the event that the penalty of suspension cannot be imposed due to [his] separation or retirement from the service." To address your queries, this Department will solely rely and focus on the facts stated in your letter and will not delve into other legal issues. Upon examination of the facts and the applicable laws and jurisprudence, this Department hereby opines in seriatim. Ombudsman Decision in Administrative Case Is Immediately Executory Regardless of an Appeal At the outset, under Section 7, Rule Ill of the Rules of Procedure of the Office of the Ombudsman, as amended by Administrative Order No. 17 dated September 15, 2003, 2 decisions of the Ombudsman in administrative cases shall be executed as a matter of course. In DILG Legal Opinion No. 134, series of 2024, this Department underscored that while the DILG may implement Ombudsman decisions, the Ombudsman itself retains its authority to directly implement and execute its decisions, which in fact occurred in this case. In Office of the Ombudsman v. Pacuribot,3 the Supreme Court held that the penalty imposed by the Ombudsman in an administrative case is immediately executory and that the filing or pendency of a6 appeal from such decision shall not stay its execution. In 1 Comelec Resolution No. 1099 dated May 24. 2024. with the subject: CALENDAR OF ACTIVITIES AND PERIODS OF CERTAIN PROHIBITED ACTS IN CONNECTION WITH THE MAY 12.2025 NATIONAL AND LOCAL ELECTIONS (NLE). AND BARMM PARLIAMENTARY ELECTIONS. 2 Section 7. Finality and execution OT decision. - Where the respondent is absolved of the charge. and in case of conviction where the penalty imposed is public censure or reprimand, suspension of not more than one month, or a fine equivalent to one month salary, the decision shall be final, executory and unappealable. In all other cases, the decision may be appealed to the Court of Appeals on a verified petition for review under the requirements and conditions set forth in Rule 43 of the Rules of Court, within fifteen (15) days from receipt of the written Notice of the Decision or Order denying the Motion for Reconsideration. An appeal shall not stop the decision from being executory. In case the penalty is suspension or removal and the respondent wins such appeal, he Shall be considered as having been under preventive suspension and shall be paid the salary and such other emoluments that he did not receive by reason of the suspension or removal. A decision of the Office of the Ombudsman in administrative cases shall be executed as a matter of course. The Office of the Ombudsman shall ensure that the decision shall be strictly enforced and properly implemented. The refusal or failure by any officer without just cause to comply with an order of the Office of the Ombudsman to remove, suspend. demote, fine, or censure shall be a ground for disciplinary action against said officer. 3 G.R. No. 193336, September 26, 2018. Page 2 of 6

Commissioner Quisumbing 'v. Executive Secretary Ochoa, et al.,4 the Supreme Court ruled that "the immediate execution of a decision of the Ombudsman is a protective measure with a purpose similar to that of preventive suspension, which is to prevent public officers from using their powers and prerogatives to influence witnesses or tamper with records." Once executed, a penalty of suspension becomes effective regardless of an appeal and the public officer ceases to have a title for the time being.5 However, it is well to point out in the said Ombudsman Rules of Procedure that a public official is considered to be on preventive suspension if (a) he appealed his administrative case before the appropriate forum, and (2) he wins such appeal. Abandonment of Condonation Doctrine; Administrative Liability is Not Extinguished Upon Re-election to the Same or Another Post The condonation doctrine, which was first edified by the Court in Pascual v. Provincial Board of Nueva Ecija prohibits the disciplining of an elective official for a wrongful act committed during his or her immediately preceding term of office. This is based on the reasoning that the said elective official's reelection is considered a condonation of his or her past misdeeds. In Carpio Morales v. Court of Appeals,6 the Court abandoned the condonation doctrine ratiocinating, inter alia, that it is "out of touch from - and now rendered obsolete by - the current legal regime." Then, in Madreo v. Bayron, the Supreme Court highlighted that the abandonment of the condonation doctrine shall be prospective in nature, or from April 12, 2016 onwards.7 The concept of public office is a public trust and the corollary requirement of accountability to the people at all times, as mandated under the 1987 Constitution, is plainly inconsistent with the idea that an elective local official's administrative liability for a misconduct committed during a prior term can be wiped off by the fact that he was elected to a second term of office, or even another elective post. Election is not a mode of condoning an administrative offense, and there is simply no constitutional or statutory basis in our jurisdiction to support the notion that an official elected for a different term is fully absolved of any administrative liability arising from an offense done during a prior term. In this jurisdiction, liability arising from administrative offenses may be condoned by the President in light of Section 19, Article VII of the 1987 Constitution xxx [.18 The Supreme Court elaborates in Office of the Ombudsman v. Vergara.9 At best, Section 66 (b) of the LGCIO prohibits the enforcement of the penalty of suspension beyond the unexpired portion of the elective local official's prior G.R. No. 214407, March 3, 2021 , s Tallado vs. Comelec, G.R. No. 246679, March 2, 2021. e Supra. Gonzaga, et al. v. Governor Garcia, et al., G.R. Nos. 201914 & 202156, April 2, 2023. e Supra. 9 G.R. No. 216871 , December 06, 2017. 10 SECTION 66. Form and Notice of Decision. — xxx (b) The penalty of suspension shall not exceed the unexpired term of the respondent or a period of six (6) months for every administrative offense, nor shall said penalty be a bar to the candidacy of the respondent so suspended as long as he meets the qualifications required for the office. xxx. Page 3 of6

term, and likewise allows said official to still run for re- election. xxx However, as previously stated, nothing in Section 66 (b) states that the elective local official's administrative liability is extinguished by the fact of re- election. Thus, at all events, no legal provision actually supports the theory that the liability is condoned. xxx It is therefore clear that administrative liability of a local elective official is not extinguished by the fact of re-election to another term of office or elective post. An administrative liability remains even if the penalty can no longer be executed after the term ends. Findings of Fact by the Ombudsman Are Generally Conclusive When Supported by Substantial Evidence and Should be Executed as a Matter of Course The Supreme Court has consistently held that the "factual findings of fact OMB are conclusive when supported by substantial evidence. Its factual findings are generally accorded with great weight and respect, if not finality by the courts, by reason of its special knowledge and expertise over matters falling under its jurisdiction. "11 Moreover, the Ombudsman Rules of Procedure states in part that a decision of the Office of the Ombudsman in administrative cases shall be executed as a matter of course. The operative phrase "matter of course" refers to something done as a part of a routine process or procedure. Stated differently, the execution of decisions of the Ombudsman in administrative cases shall be made part and parcel of standard procedure, regardless of the availment of remedies therefrom, and was already clarified by the Ombudsman Rules of Procedure. Therefore, decisions of the Ombudsman must be implemented immediately and without regard to whether they have attained finality. Legal Effect of SP Victor's Suspension as Outgoing SP in his Assumption to Office as the Newly-Elected Mayor of Bugasong, Antique The suspension order against outgoing SP Victor retains its legal effect and remains in force in his capacity as the newly-elected Mayor. As clarified, the suspension imposed by the Ombudsman attaches to SP Victor, irrespective of his election to a Mayor position. Notably, under Section 46(a) of Republic Act No. 716012, suspension from office constitutes a temporary vacancy in the office of the local chief executive. A temporary vacancy entails a situation where the office is not permanently vacated, and the incumbent is expected to return upon the end of suspension or incapacity. Therefore, in case of temporary incapacity of the mayor, either physical or legal reasons, the vice- mayor shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties of the local chief 11 Cabrera v. The Honorable Office of the Ombudsman. et al, G.R. No. 248842, January 22, 2025. 12 Otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991. " Page 4 of 6

executive. The assumption of the acting mayor is by operation of law and there is no need for appointment before said official performs the duties and functions of the office. As such, since SP Victor is decreed suspended by virtue of the Ombudsman decision dated March 7, 2025, he cannot therefore assume office on June 30, 2025 as the newly-elected Mayor of Bugasong, Antique regardless of an appeal he availed, or might avail of. Such being the case, the elected Vice-Mayor of Bugasong, Antique after taking an oath of office as Vice-Mayor at noon of June 30, 2025 shall perform the duties and functions of the Mayor, albeit in an acting capacity pursuant to Section 445 (a) (4) of RA 7160, until the expiration of the suspension period, or unless he filed an appropriate legal remedy and the competent court resolves otherwise. While we truly understand your concern about the status for the Mayor position of Bugasong, Antique by June 30, 2025, we would just like to emphasize that In DILG Opinion No. 21 , Series of 2009, we clarified that our opinion is merely persuasive in nature and not binding to the courts. Thus: "At the outset, please be informed that our opinions are not binding to the courts of law. Instead, it is the other way around. Being part of the executive branch of the government, we are primarily tasked to interpret them. This means that while we may render opinion regarding a certain law, our opinion thereon is never binding to any court of law. At most, our opinion only has a persuasive effect. Thus, if a court of law, especially our Supreme Court, has already interpreted a particular law through a decision it rendered in a case, we are bound thereby and obliged to observe them in our subsequent actions involving substantially similar issues and/or facts." As pointed out by the Supreme Court in Tallado v. Comelec, the DILG's opinion on what provision of the LGC properly applied was far from binding or controlling. It was even irrelevant. 13 Nevertheless, this opinion is rendered solely for academic discussion purposes, without prejudice to any contrary interpretation that may be issued by competent authorities or the courts or to any supervening developments arising from the resolution of any legal remedies which may have been or may still be resorted to. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Respectfully yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P.
